editor_note: Routine appointee interviews; no specific closed-session topic.
headline: SLC Council interviews utilities board and Planning Commission appointees; closed session possible
title: Salt Lake City Council Work Session Agenda
why_it_matters: At its Oct. 6 work session the council interviews Landon Kraczek for the Planning Commission and John Milliken and Clarence Verhoef for the Public Utilities Advisory Board. The agenda also lists a tentative closed meeting under the standard statutory reasons; no specific topic is given.

editor_note: Duplicates impact fee item pmn:1107993, which carries the specific numbers.
headline: SLC Council to vote on first utility impact fee hike since 1999, budget amendment
title: Salt Lake City Council Formal Meeting Agenda
why_it_matters: On Oct. 6 the council may vote on the first water, sewer and stormwater impact fee increase since 1999. It also takes up Budget Amendment No. 1, which includes $11.5 million in grants for Fleet Block and 9 Line improvements and a $700,000 transfer for the Old Library Building. Public hearings cover banning community correctional facilities and jails citywide, a contested Ellerbeck Mansion rezoning, an airport wetland sale to the state and a liquor proximity waiver for Taste of Thai.

headline: Hearing on rezoning 10th East Senior Center and Victory Park to public lands
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Zoning Map Amendment at Approximately 237 & 239 S 1000 East
why_it_matters: An Oct. 6 hearing covers rezoning city-owned land at 237 and 239 South 1000 East from SR-3 and R-2 to PL. The site holds the 10th East Senior Center and Victory Park, and the change would match zoning to the existing public use.

editor_note: Same Oct. 6 council meeting as the impact fee story; keep fee item as lead.
headline: Salt Lake City weighs banning new community correctional facilities and jails
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Community Correctional Facilities and Jails Text Amendment
why_it_matters: An Oct. 6 hearing covers removing community correctional facilities and jails as conditional uses, which would make them prohibited citywide. State- and federally owned property would be exempt.

headline: SLC to write Affordable Housing Incentives fines directly into zoning code
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Affordable Housing Incentives Fines Text Amendment
why_it_matters: An Oct. 6 hearing covers adding fines for the Affordable Housing Incentives program to Chapter 21A.20. The zoning code currently points to a fee schedule that lists no fines, so this closes an enforcement gap for every property using the program.

headline: Taste of Thai seeks liquor proximity waiver near Sprague Library
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Waiver of Proximity for Taste of Thai at 2130 South Highland Drive
why_it_matters: An Oct. 6 hearing covers a waiver for Taste of Thai Restaurant at 2130 South Highland Drive, which sits across from Sprague Library. Under a state law in effect since May 2026, cities must approve such waivers before DABS can grant a liquor license.

editor_note: Contested rezoning, but a single Avenues parcel hearing is a brief.
headline: Ellerbeck Mansion owners seek rezoning to expand cafe into neighboring Avenues home
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Zoning Map and General Plan Amendment at Approximately 140 North B Street and 272 East 3rd Avenue
why_it_matters: Kara and Tyler Alden want 140 North B Street and 272 East 3rd Avenue rezoned from RMF-35 to MU-2 so they can expand cafe and retail uses. The Planning Commission recommended against converting the single-family home, citing loss of housing and impacts on neighbors; the hearing is Oct. 6.

headline: SLC may waive payment for Great Salt Lake conservation easement to Utah Open Lands
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Conservation Easement Public Benefit Analysis
why_it_matters: An Oct. 6 hearing covers a resolution waiving any amounts due for a conservation easement over city-owned parcels next to the Great Salt Lake. The easement would go to Utah Open Lands.

editor_note: Same Oct. 6 council meeting; wetland sale is useful but secondary to impact fees.
headline: Airport to sell about 951 acres of wetlands to state for waterfowl area
title: Notice of Public Hearing on Wetland Mitigation Disposition of Significant Parcel
why_it_matters: The Department of Airports proposes selling surplus wetland mitigation land of about 951 acres to the Utah Department of Natural Resources for a waterfowl management area. Appraisals put the land at roughly $3.8 million to $5.1 million, with the easement valued up to $571,000; the required hearing is Oct. 6.

headline: SLC utility impact fees would roughly triple; first increase since 1999
title: Public Hearing on Public Utilities Impact Fee Facilities Plan, Impact Fee Analysis, and Consolidated Fee Schedule
why_it_matters: The proposal would raise the water impact fee for a 3/4-inch meter from $1,871 to $5,577 and the stormwater fee per quarter acre from $374 to $1,993. It also adds a meter-based sewer fee of $4,300 for a 3/4-inch meter. Fees would phase in at 70% from Jan. 1, 2027, and reach full amounts July 1, 2028; the council hearing and possible vote are Oct. 6.

editor_note: Planning Commission agenda preview; Lamplighter rezoning is the lead item but meeting is a routine step.
headline: Planning Commission weighs Lamplighter Square rezoning and citywide housing options change
title: SLC Planning Commission Agenda for September 23, 2026
why_it_matters: TP Lamplighter LC seeks MU-3 zoning on Foothill Drive and 1700 South for retail, offices and 19 townhomes, and wants the city removed from the Lamplighter Square CC&Rs. The commission also continues its hearing on the citywide Expanding Housing Options amendment for small-lot dwellings in low-density zones. Other items are a rezoning at 1469 W California Ave and a 16-unit mixed-use building replacing a donut shop at 950 W 1000 N.

editor_note: Board meeting already happened; outcomes are useful but not a new call-today story.
headline: Inland Port expands Black Gold area, tables Iron Springs power campus amid data center criticism
title: Utah Inland Port Authority (UIPA) Board Meeting
why_it_matters: The board adopted the Black Gold amendment adding 8,598 acres in Roosevelt and the Pony Express amendment. It tabled the Iron Springs amendment, which includes the Juniper zone planned for a rail-served industrial and power campus. Public commenters urged a moratorium on data centers, and staff reported 135 acres of the North Temple Landfill remediated, with a plat for 171 developable acres submitted to Salt Lake City.

editor_note: Bond already known and set for Nov. 3 ballot; hearing is a routine step.
headline: Salt Lake County hearing on $128 million parks and open space bond
title: Public Bond Hearing and Meeting
why_it_matters: On Oct. 6 the county council takes public comment on issuing up to $128 million in general obligation bonds for open space, parks, trails and recreation facilities. Voters decide the bond in a Nov. 3, 2026, special election.

editor_note: Audit presentation is worth a look; budget items are routine. Not a call-today record.
headline: County auditor presents audit of Discovery Gateway oversight
title: County Council Meeting
why_it_matters: At the Oct. 6 meeting the county auditor presents a performance audit of the county's oversight of the Discovery Gateway agreement. The council also votes on 2027 employee benefits and on budget shifts, including $646,000 for higher Adobe and Microsoft licensing costs and $1.68 million for landfill methane flare design and fencing.

editor_note: Meeting already held; Salt Palace cancellations are worth a brief, not urgent calls.
headline: County cancels $19.8M in Salt Palace projects; reviews jail expansion feasibility study
names: Larry H. and Gail Miller Arts Center
title: County Council Meeting
why_it_matters: The Sept. 29 agenda would cancel $19.8 million in Salt Palace capital projects and redirect $11 million to debt service on renovation bonds. It also cancels $3.9 million in operating subsidy and $5 million in client relief funding. The council heard a jail expansion feasibility study from Babcock Design Group and voted to add security to the 2026 transient room tax bonds.

editor_note: Meeting already held, routine bond election and ethics steps.
headline: County sets Nov. 3 bond election rules, adopts ethics disclosure ordinance
title: County Council Meeting
why_it_matters: At its Sept. 22 meeting the county council considered a resolution on conducting the Nov. 3 special bond election and final adoption of conflict-of-interest disclosure rules for county officers. Other items included $824,690 a year to operate the new South Jordan competition pool, a $320,000 land purchase in Draper from the state and a UTA presentation.

editor_note: Routine liquor commission business; violation settlements are a brief at most.
headline: Liquor commission cites Dave & Buster's, approves Hopkins Brewing and new licenses
title: Commission Meeting
why_it_matters: Violation settlements include Dave & Buster's, Sakura Hibachi, Caffe Molise and Handosake in Salt Lake City. The commission also took up a package agency for Hopkins Brewing Company and licenses for Henry Baker, Via Veneto Pizzarium, BGR Burgers and Pantry Box in Salt Lake City, plus a bar license for Nicklaus Turnhouse in Park City. A new deputy commissioner was to be appointed.
